note: Railway Budget (separate from the Union Budget until its merger in 2017): the merger year and the separate-budget history are in neither the Constitution text nor NCERT Chapter 5 as fetched for this chapter. Source gap; not taught.
Taught: a Money Bill / financial Bill on Article 110(1)(a)-(f) matters cannot be introduced without the recommendation of the President (Article 117(1)).
Taught: same as WBCS 2016 Q47 — Article 117(1) President's recommendation for a Money Bill.
Taught: the Public Accounts Committee has 15 members from the Lok Sabha (and 7 from the Rajya Sabha; 22 in total).
Taught: passage of a Money Bill does not require the Rajya Sabha's approval — it can only recommend within 14 days (Article 109); joint sitting is also not applicable.
Taught: the Rajya Sabha cannot amend a Money Bill; its changes are only recommendations which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject (Article 109). Chapter carries an exam_note on exactly this question.
Taught: statement 1 is false — the PAC has 15 Lok Sabha members, not 25; the chapter teaches the PAC's composition (15+7=22) and its examination of appropriation accounts and CAG reports.
Taught: whether a Bill is a Money Bill is finally determined by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha (Article 110(3)).

Not taught: PAC members are elected by proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote — this election method is in the Lok Sabha Rules (sansad.in handbook), which is outside the validator-allowed sources fetched for this chapter (Constitution, NCERT, cag.gov.in). The chapter teaches PAC composition and functions only. Source gap disclosed.

Not taught: the convention that the PAC Chairperson comes from the Opposition is not stated in any source fetched for this chapter (the CAG page and NCERT are silent on the Chairperson). Convention not in allowed sources; not taught.
Taught: Bills other than Money Bills may be introduced in either House of Parliament (Article 107(1)).
Taught: parliamentary authorisation is necessary prior to expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India (Article 266(3) read with Article 114).

Taught: all revenues, loans raised and loan repayments received by the Union Government flow into the Consolidated Fund of India (Article 266(1)). Chapter carries an exam_note on exactly this question.
Taught: the Speaker of the Lok Sabha decides whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not (Article 110(3)).
